Aldrich Ames was a CIA analyst and Moscow station chief who became the most damaging mole in American intelligence history. For nine years, he sold secrets to the Soviet Union and Russia, compromising dozens of intelligence operations and costing the lives of at least a dozen American assets abroad.

Ames joined the CIA in nineteen sixty-two with access to classified information about American intelligence operations, agents, and spy techniques across decades of Cold War espionage. Then, in nineteen eighty-five while working at CIA headquarters in Arlington, he began spying for the Soviet Union. He was initially motivated by financial desperation—a failing marriage, mortgage debt—and a desire for attention.

He provided the Soviets with detailed information about CIA operations, agent identities, and technical methods. In exchange, he earned approximately two point seven million dollars while exposing dozens of American assets. His compromises led to the execution or imprisonment of at least ten CIA assets in the Soviet Union, undermining American intelligence gathering during a critical period.

For nine years, Ames remained undetected, living in relative comfort while colleagues and superiors overlooked the signs of his treason. The FBI finally arrested him in February nineteen ninety-four after an intensive investigation. He was convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment without parole. He remains incarcerated today, having never shown remorse for the agents he betrayed.
